title:
From field readings
to a report draft.
sub: Without retyping the same data in the office.
caption: A reporting workflow built around your forms and your review process.

title:
The inspection is done.
The reporting work isn’t.
sub: Readings, photos and follow-up questions can still be spread across separate files.
caption: Start with one handoff: from the technician’s record to the office’s draft.

title:
1. Reuse the site details.
Record fresh results.
sub: The site and system are already identified. New reading fields start empty.
caption: Previous readings are a reference. They do not become today’s results.

title:
Enter the readings
once, on site.
sub: Here, the technician records the waterflow alarm time and main drain readings.
caption: These sample entries will populate the draft report.

title:
2. Keep the finding
with the inspection.
sub: Attach the photo, location and field note to the same record.
caption: This sample finding is a painted sprinkler in Room 214.

title:
The office gets a draft
from those entries.
sub: The same readings and finding appear in the report.
caption: The report is still a draft. It has not been approved or sent.

title:
3. Review the source
before release.
sub: Open the submitted record to check what the technician entered.
caption: Office amendments are recorded separately, with a reason for the change.

title:
Missing a detail?
Ask on the same record.
sub: The reviewer asks where the sprinkler is located within Room 214.
caption: The question goes back with the inspection, ready for the technician to answer.

title:
The technician gets
the review note.
sub: Add the missing location and resubmit the inspection.
caption: The office receives the updated field record and can review it again.

title:
Approve the report.
Keep the finding open.
sub: After review, release the report to the customer view.
caption: Approving the report does not mean the deficiency has been repaired.

title:
The report stays
with the system.
sub: Open this year’s report or return to a previous inspection.
caption: One site, one system and its inspection history.

title:
See it with
your own form.
sub: Send one inspection form and a sample customer report.
caption: Free one-form example within 3 business days. I’ll flag complex forms up front.
